rationale: C has no export construct -- no keyword, no module, no visibility attribute -- so an `exports` edge in C can only ever describe a CONVENTION, and #963 pinned that convention to five macro NAMES. A name list is the same defect every time: right about the codebases it was written from, silent about the next one. Measured over 359 sqlite C/H files with `script/m14/tmp/c-audit/c-ontology-verdicts.ts`: the corpus defines SEVEN marker names and the five-name list matches NONE of them, so `exports` fired 0 times on that corpus. Two of the seven are `extern` markers the analyzer had never heard of -- `autosetup/jimsh0.c:723 #define JIM_EXPORT extern` and `ext/wasm/libcmpp.c:104,111 #define CMPP_EXPORT extern` / `... extern __declspec(dllexport)` -- carrying 274 declarations. The structural half of the convention is derivable with no list: a macro whose replacement list OPENS with the linkage keyword `extern` contributes linkage and nothing else, so every declaration it prefixes is externally linked. This rule reads the file's own `preproc_def` nodes, same-file only (C-D2). THE REFUSALS ARE THE POINT and each is a real corpus shape: `ext/wasm/libcmpp.c:5256 #define CMPP_PRIVATE static` (52 declarations that are INTERNAL linkage -- the opposite marker), `src/mutex_unix.c:39,41 #define ALIGN128` (an alignment attribute on one branch, nothing on the other), `src/sqliteInt.h:1329,1335 #define SQLITE_WSD` (thread-local). All three are EMPTY replacement lists. An empty macro contributes no tokens, so STRUCTURE cannot tell what it means -- only its NAME can, and the name is the list this change removes. 58 declarations ride the empty branch on this corpus and at least 52 are not exports. The genuine empty-marker case in this corpus is sqlite's own `SQLITE_API` (`src/sqlite.h.in:75`) and it is unreachable per-file anyway: `sqlite3.h` is GENERATED at build time, so no corpus file defines it. The controls are the five #963 conventions, which must keep working (the list is still required for markers defined in another header -- the kernel macros live in a file this analyzer never reads), and the platform-varied marker, where `#ifdef` picks the replacement list and both branches are `extern`.

Deciding it by name is the fixed list this change removes, and sqlite's own genuine empty marker `SQLITE_API` is unreachable per-file because `sqlite3.h` is generated at build time.
